passages.scripture: Come now, you who are rich, weep and wail over the misery to come upon you.

lines.text: This message is for people who are rich.
You who are rich, listen now.
You will face misery soon.
Weep because of this misery.
Wail loudly because trouble is coming to you.

passages.scripture: Your riches have rotted and moths have eaten your clothes.

lines.text: James addresses these rich people.
Your riches have rotted.
Moths have eaten your clothes.

passages.scripture: Your gold and silver are corroded. Their corrosion will testify against you and consume your flesh like fire. You have hoarded treasure in the last days.

lines.text: There are rich people with gold and silver.
They have hoarded treasure in the last days.
Their gold is corroded.
Their silver is corroded.
The corrosion of their gold and silver will stand as a witness against them.
This corrosion will consume your flesh like fire.

passages.scripture: Look, the wages you withheld from the workmen who mowed your fields are crying out against you. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.

lines.text: These rich people had workers who worked for them.
These workers mowed the fields of the rich people.
But these rich people withheld wages from the workers who mowed their fields.
These unpaid wages are crying out against these rich people.
These rich people had harvesters work for them.
But these rich people treated their harvesters with injustice.
The harvesters are crying out because of this injustice.
The Lord of Hosts hears their cries.

passages.scripture: You have lived on earth in luxury and self-indulgence. You have fattened your hearts in the day of slaughter.

lines.text: These rich people lived their life on earth.
These rich people lived in luxury.
These rich people lived in self-indulgence.
And so these rich people fattened their hearts.
These rich people did this for the day of slaughter.

passages.scripture: You have condemned and murdered the righteous, who did not resist you.

lines.text: These rich people condemned the righteous person.
These rich people murdered the righteous person.
The righteous person did not resist them.

passages.scripture: Be patient, then, brothers, until the Lord’s coming. See how the farmer awaits the precious fruit of the soil—how patient he is for the fall and spring rains.

lines.text: Therefore, James encourages his brothers to be patient.
Wait until the Lord comes.
The Lord will return.
As an analogy, look at a farmer.
A farmer waits for the valuable fruit of the earth.
A farmer is patient.
A farmer waits for the early rain.
And a farmer waits for the late rain.
A farmer does not hurry.
A farmer trusts the right time will come.

passages.scripture: You, too, be patient and strengthen your hearts, because the Lord’s coming is near.

lines.text: The Lord will come soon.
Therefore we must be patient.
We must make our hearts strong.
We must do this because the Lord’s coming is near.

passages.scripture: Do not complain about one another, brothers, so that you will not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door!

lines.text: Brothers, do not complain about one another.
If you complain, you may be judged.
The Judge is standing at the door.

passages.scripture: Brothers, as an example of patience in affliction, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

lines.text: Brothers, listen carefully.
I want you to look at the prophets who came before us.
These prophets spoke in the name of the Lord.
They suffered many hardships.
They showed great patience during their suffering.
Let the prophets be your example of patience in affliction.

passages.scripture: See how blessed we consider those who have persevered. You have heard of Job’s perseverance and have seen the outcome from the Lord. The Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

lines.text: We call people blessed when they persevere.
You have heard about Job.
Job showed great perseverance.
You have seen what the Lord did for Job in the end.
The Lord is very compassionate.
The Lord is merciful.

passages.scripture: Above all, my brothers, do not swear, not by heaven or earth or by any other oath. Simply let your “Yes” be yes, and your “No,” no, so that you will not fall under judgment.

lines.text: Brothers, I speak to you now.
This is most important.
Do not swear any oaths.
Do not swear by heaven.
Do not swear by earth.
Do not swear by anything else.
Let your “Yes” mean yes.
Let your “No” mean no.
If you do this, you will not fall under judgment.

passages.scripture: Is any one of you suffering? He should pray. Is anyone cheerful? He should sing praises.

lines.text: If anyone among you is suffering, he should pray.
If anyone among you is cheerful, he should sing praises.

passages.scripture: Is any one of you sick? He should call the elders of the church to pray over him and anoint him with oil in the name of the Lord.

lines.text: If any one of you is sick, he should act.
He should call the elders of the church.
The elders should come to him.
The elders should pray over him.
The elders should anoint him with oil.
The elders should do this in the name of the Lord.

passages.scripture: And the prayer offered in faith will restore the one who is sick. The Lord will raise him up. If he has sinned, he will be forgiven.

lines.text: The prayer offered in faith will restore the sick person.
The Lord will raise him up.
If the sick person has sinned, God will forgive him.

passages.scripture: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous man has great power to prevail.

lines.text: Confess your sins to each other.
Pray for each other.
God will heal you.
A righteous person prays with power.
The prayer of a righteous person is very effective.

passages.scripture: Elijah was a man just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years.

lines.text: Elijah was a man.
He was just like us.
Elijah prayed earnestly.
He asked that it would not rain.
Then, it did not rain on the land.
This lasted for three and a half years.

passages.scripture: Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth yielded its crops.

lines.text: Elijah was a man just like us.
He prayed again.
God answered his prayer.
Then the sky gave rain.
And the earth produced its crops.

passages.scripture: My brothers, if one of you should wander from the truth and someone should bring him back, consider this: Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way will save his soul from death and cover over a multitude of sins.

lines.text: Brothers, I speak to you now.
Some of you may wander away from the truth.
Someone among you may bring that person back.
Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way saves that sinner’s soul from death.
He also covers a multitude of sins.
